page_title: Free Video Upscaler: Upscale Video with AI, No Upload | ToHD

sources.entry: ToHD - Free AI video upscaler that runs in the browser on your own GPU (WebGPU): turns 360p/480p clips into 720p or 1080p without uploading them, no signup, no watermark. #freemium #video

summary.name: ToHD
summary.one_liner: A free AI video upscaler that runs entirely in the browser on the user's own GPU via WebGPU, turning 360p/480p MP4, MOV or WebM clips into 720p or 1080p without uploading the video.
use_cases: Making low-resolution phone or camera clips 720p or 1080p
Upscaling anime episodes or clips to HD
Sharpening soft or slightly out of focus footage
Restoring old VHS or camcorder video
Upscaling private family or work footage without uploading it
Converting 1080p footage to 4K with cloud processing
summary.what_it_does: The tool decodes, upscales and re-encodes a video inside the browser tab using WebGPU, so the file is not sent to a server. It runs open source Real-ESRGAN models, with a general model for camera footage and an animation model selected via an Anime mode. Before a full run it upscales a few frames to measure the device's speed and show a time estimate. The output downloads as an MP4 that keeps the original audio track. Optional paid cloud processing runs the same models on remote GPUs for faster speed, longer clips, batches and 4K, and also offers background noise reduction and restoration features.
notable: Processes video locally in the browser via WebGPU, with no upload and no install
Tests a few frames first to show the expected processing time on the user's computer
Anime mode uses the realesr-animevideov3 model
Minimal in-browser pipeline is open source on GitHub under MIT license
caveats: Free in-browser speed depends on the device; laptops with integrated graphics can be 5 to 10 times slower, and long clips are slow
Best supported in recent desktop Chrome or Edge; no mention of Firefox or Safari support
Cloud processing is paid, starting from $5 in credit packs, and uploads the video to a server
4K in the browser takes a while on most computers
